subject: Subprocessor addition notice: DataMesh onboarding + order form implication
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@cloudarray.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: legalops@cloudarray.com, tom.hsu@procurement.cloudarray.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice — onboarding DataMesh as a subprocessor (Order Form implications)

Hi Rafael,

Quick heads-up: CloudArray is onboarding DataMesh (data-mesh.ai) as a downstream subprocessor for log ingestion and long-term storage for the DW-1482 engagement. Per our MSA Section 5.2, we’re sending formal notice plus the proposed DPA and a short SOC2 summary.

Attachments: DataMesh-DPA-proposal.pdf, DataMesh-SOC2-summary.pdf.

A couple of points to flag:
- DataMesh requires a minor change to the Order Form to add an "edge storage" line item that increases monthly fees by ~8% for the connected ingestion pipeline.
- DataMesh will be subject to the flow-down clause we proposed; they can sign a DPA and accept flowdown obligations.

Can you confirm routing and whether Redwood needs additional evidence (full SOC2 report, encrypted key custody statement, or contractual amendments) to accept DataMesh as a subprocessor? We can provide a short SOC2 snapshot and limited evidence this week.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Legal Operations
CloudArray Inc.

---

To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Notice — onboarding DataMesh as a subprocessor (Order Form implications)

Team — forwarding the CloudArray notice. Key asks: legal review for DPA and flow-down adequacy; procurement review for the ~8% price delta on the Order Form.

Immediate questions:
- Kimberly: assuming DataMesh signs the DPA and we get SOC2 summary, do we need redline changes to the MSA beyond the standard flowdown language? Any mandatory language (e.g., audit rights, subprocessor termination) we should insist on?
- Neha / Marissa: what is our threshold for accepting a price increase at this stage without escalating to leadership? This is an existing live account (DW-1482) and CloudArray requests a fast turn here.

Samantha — can you confirm timeline for SOC2 evidence and a link to the signed DPA once available?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, samantha.ortiz@cloudarray.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Notice — onboarding DataMesh as a subprocessor (Order Form implications)

Rafael — thanks for the ping. I reviewed the attached DPA and SOC2 summary quickly; high-level notes below. I attached a short redline to the Order Form and a one-page comment memo (see OrderForm-CloudArray-Redline.docx).

Legal assessment (quick take):
- DPA: DataMesh's proposed DPA is mostly acceptable, but we need explicit audit rights in the flow-down, and a clause that requires immediate notification of any security incident impacting Redwood-origin data within 48 hours. Please ask CloudArray to ensure DataMesh agrees to these flow-down specifics.
- Subprocessor termination: we should include a fallback clause allowing Redwood to suspend DataMesh access if remediation isn't completed within a 30-day remediation window.
- Data residency: if DataMesh intends to store logs outside of the US, add an explicit residency/transfer paragraph; otherwise require encryption-at-rest with key management details.

Procurement note: the 8% uplift should be documented in an amendment to the Order Form with a firm start date and a trial period for the ingestion workload.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Request: CloudArray / DataMesh to sign the DPA with the two redlines (audit-rights + 48-hour incident notif).
2) Request: Provide full SOC2 Type II report or at minimum a SOC2 bridge letter. SOC2 summary alone is insufficient for our acceptance threshold on live production ingestion.
3) Procurement to review price delta; if under the $100k ARR threshold we can approve; otherwise route to finance for sign-off.

I'm available for a 30-min call this afternoon if helpful.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

- DataMesh is willing to accept the audit-rights flow-down and the 48-hour incident notification. They have proposed slightly different language for the remediation window; we can ask them to accept Redwood’s 30-day remediation window.
- We can provide the full SOC2 Type II report under an NDA. If Redwood can confirm standard mutual NDA usage, we’ll share by end of day Friday.
- On pricing: the 8% change is a permanent uplift to the ingestion line item. Tom (cc'd) can provide the procurement amendment and DocuSign envelope.

DocuSign envelope (order form amendment): https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789
Drive folder with evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-CloudArray-DPAs

Please advise if the above addresses Kimberly’s redlines; DataMesh confirms they will sign the redlined DPA once language is finalized.

Best,
CloudArray LegalOps

- Is the 8% uplift acceptable under our current ARR threshold? If not, what sign-off path/time will we need?
- If we accept, can procurement please confirm the draft amendment (DocuSign envelope) will include a 90-day trial clause and a rollback mechanism if ingestion costs exceed forecast?

Samantha — please hold the DocuSign until procurement confirms the administrative language.

Rafael — reviewed. Procurement position: we can absorb up to a 6% uplift without exec escalation for DW-1482. 8% exceeds the threshold and requires approval by Finance (VP of Revenue Ops) — estimate 2 business days for decision if we route today.

Conditions to accept quickly without further escalation:
- DataMesh signs the redlined DPA (audit rights + 48-hour incident notification + 30-day remediation).
- CloudArray provides SOC2 Type II under NDA by EOD Friday.
- Amendment includes a 90-day trial/rollback clause (if ingestion costs materially exceed forecast).

If CloudArray can (1) and (2) within the timeline, Procurement will approve a temporary exception while we route to Finance. If not, we need to pause the DocuSign envelope.

I'll prepare a one-page procurement consent memo to expedite Finance review if needed.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference
